structure.overview: This case concerns the assessment of costs following the Federal Court of Appeal's dismissal of the Appellant's appeal against Canada. The Respondent, Canada, filed a Bill of Costs which the Appellant did not oppose, leading the court to assess and allow the costs claimed by the Respondent. The court allowed the full amount of $2,750.23 in costs and disbursements to be paid by the Appellant.

party_points.text: Respondent informed costs settled, assessment not needed
Respondent later advised costs not settled, requested resumption
Respondent filed costs materials; Appellant filed none

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: This paragraph introduces the costs assessment following the Federal Court of Appeal's dismissal of the Appellant's appeal with costs on December 12, 2017.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Costs will be assessed according to Rule 407 of the Federal Courts Rules, which mandates party-and-party costs per Tariff B unless the Court orders otherwise.

citations.cite: Rule 407 of the Federal Courts Rules, SOR/98-106 (FCR)
citations.why: States the rule governing costs assessment.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Respondent filed a Bill of Costs on February 27, 2020.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Due to COVID-19 and suspended filing deadlines, the Federal Court of Appeal issued a direction on June 19, 2020, setting filing dates for costs assessment documents.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Respondent informed the court on August 31, 2020, that costs had been settled and assessment was no longer needed.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: On November 10, 2020, the Respondent advised the court that costs were not settled and requested resumption of assessment; the court directed accordingly.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Respondent filed costs materials on February 27 and November 10, 2020; the Appellant filed no responding material.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Appellant did not respond to the Respondent's costs claim, leaving it largely unopposed; the court cites Dahl v. Canada on assessment officer's role.
idea_list: Court cites Dahl v. Canada on assessment officer's neutrality and limits

citations.cite: Dahl v. Canada, 2007 FC 192, at paragraph 2
citations.why: Explains assessment officer's role when costs are unopposed.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court cites Carlile v. Canada emphasizing taxing officers must balance avoiding unnecessary costs and indemnifying real costs.
idea_list: Carlile v. Canada on taxing officers' duties

citations.cite: Carlile v. Canada, [1997] F.C.J. No. 885, at paragraph 26
citations.why: Guidance on taxing officers' balancing duties.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Despite no challenge from the Appellant, the court must ensure Respondent's cost claims are necessary and reasonable using all relevant materials.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Respondent claims $2,450.00 for assessable services.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the Respondent's claimed assessable services necessary and reasonable and allows the full $2,450.00.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Respondent claims $347.54 in disbursements.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court allows $72.86 for process serving, finding it necessary and reasonable.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes issues with the Respondent's photocopying claims and will review them further.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds inadequate detail on photocopying claims, allowing only one copy each of the Appeal Book and Appellant’s Memorandum, citing Merck & Co. v. Apotex.
idea_list: Only one copy allowed for reimbursement
Cites Merck & Co. v. Apotex on assessment discretion

citations.cite: Merck & Co. v. Apotex, 2008 FCA 371, at paragraph 14
citations.why: Explains discretion in determining reasonable expenses.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court cites Bujnowski v. Canada to deny reimbursement for copies of documents already provided by the Appellant.
idea_list: Bujnowski v. Canada on denying reimbursement for provided copies

citations.cite: Bujnowski v. Canada, [2010] FCJ No 346, at paragraph 34
citations.why: Supports denying costs for copies already provided.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Following Merck and Bujnowski, the court allows only one copy each of the Appeal Book and Memorandum, totaling $23.66.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court allows photocopying costs for the Respondent’s Memorandum and Joint Book of Authorities as reasonable and necessary.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court totals the allowed disbursements at $300.23.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Respondent’s Bill of Costs is allowed in full at $2,750.23, payable by the Appellant; a Certificate of Assessment will be issued.
